To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated the genomic fragment that encodes the antigen defined by the monoclonal antibody and that we have found the cosmid vector to be unsuitable for the long‐term expression of the antigen.

a monoclonal antibody‐selected cosmid shuttle vector system is a useful tool for isolating the genomic DNA controlling a specific antigen expression and that a 34. 8 kb DNA fragment isolated from this system is responsible for the antigen‐positive phenotype.
we have cloned the genomic DNA responsible for the expression of a specific melanoma antigen defined by monoclonal antibody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of genomic DNA controlling the melanoma‐specific antigen defined by monoclonal antibody.
a new strategy to isolate genomic DNA controlling the antigen expression by the use of a shuttle vector and a monoclonal antibody and with a novel instability of the insert DNA in the vector.
the isolation of genomic DNA controlling the antigen expression by the use of monoclonal antibody and with the instability of the antigen‐positive clones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we isolated the genomic DNA responsible for the expression of mouse melanoma antigen by the cosmid shuttle vector system.
we have isolated and characterized the genomic DNA controlling mouse melanoma antigen defined by monoclonal antibody.
we have isolated the DNA controlling the expression, but not the DNA coding for the antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmid vector system is useful in isolation of genomic DNA controlling the antigen expression, but the vector itself should be improved to avoid the instability of the insert DNA.
we could isolate the genomic DNA controlling melanoma antigen by the combination of cosmid library, monoclonal antibody, and cell sorting.
we have isolated the genomic fragment controlling the antigen expression and that the fragment may be used as a selectable gene for the gene therapy of human melanomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cosmid vector used in our study is not a suitable vehicle to rescue genomic DNA controlling the cell surface antigen expression.
the instability of the antigen‐positive cells is not due to the instability of the genomic DNA controlling antigen expression.
the cosmid vector is useful for isolating a genomic DNA controlling antigen expression, provided that the vector sequence is not lost from the transfectant.
